methodology: Findings were produced by two independent close-reading passes over the full expedition-window Captain's Log text (Days 1-21, then Days 22-42, chronologically), cross-checking the second pass against the first pass's registry so cross-batch repetition could be detected. Excerpts below are kept to a single sentence or short phrase per finding, per the audit's public-safety constraint; full paragraph-length source text is not reproduced here. No source content was edited. NOTE: day numbers cited in the 'days' fields below are the ORIGINAL Facebook-post-labeled day numbers, not canonical website Day numbers — see day-number-mapping.json for the translation table (only original label 13 requires special handling, since it splits into canonical Days 13 and 14).

excerpts: Day 10 primary (Ch. 8): "A hundred-dollar dinner isn't simply a hundred-dollar dinner... We've slowly stopped measuring money in dollars. We measure it in days."
Day 10 same-day aside ('Wealth'): "A hundred-dollar dinner isn't simply a hundred-dollar dinner... We've stopped measuring money in dollars. We measure it in time."
findings.explanation: The Day 10 primary entry and its same-day supplemental 'Wealth' aside make the identical argument with the identical central image within hours of each other.

excerpts: "We've stopped measuring money in dollars. We measure it in time." (Day 10)
"Money is time's shadow." (Day 15)
findings.explanation: The 'money is really time' thesis gets a full second two-chapter treatment on Day 15, five days after being fully argued on Day 10.

excerpts: "Texas had taught us to begin... Glacier, Banff, and Jasper taught us humility." (Day 11)
"We covered this yesterday, but..." (Day 12, Ch. 3 — self-acknowledged repeat, then repeats anyway)
findings.explanation: The same state-by-state route recap is given four times within two days, including one instance where the text itself flags the repeat and continues anyway.

excerpts: idx51 wakes at Kluane Lake, Yukon and ends "Welcome to Alaska."
idx53 wakes "beside a river near Copper Center, Alaska" (already inside the state).
findings.explanation: Two posts both self-label Day 13 but describe sequential, non-overlapping geography — very likely a mislabeled day number requiring resequencing, not a genuine same-day double narrative.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED by human editorial decision (see facebook-import-manifest.md revision history). Original Day numbers are not authoritative; the canonical sequence is built from narrative chronology instead. idx51 becomes canonical Day 13 (Kluane Lake -> Alaska border) and idx53 becomes canonical Day 14 (Copper Center -> McCarthy Road), per the confirmed geographic sequence. See day-number-mapping.json for the full original-to-canonical translation table.

excerpts: "Patience catches more salmon than power ever will." (Day 16)
"The river hadn't changed. I had... It rewards patience." (Day 17)
findings.explanation: The same 'fishing rewards patience over force' lesson is explained at near-full length on two consecutive days.

excerpts: "Some places measure time by clocks. Alaska measures it by light." (Day 15)
findings.explanation: The midnight-sun/disoriented-time observation is explained in full on Day 12, then re-explained as a reflective aside on Day 15, and resurfaces as stated observation through Days 20-21.

excerpts: "The vacation quietly ended." (Day 11)
"The expedition stopped feeling like a vacation. It started feeling like a life." (Day 16)
findings.explanation: The 'this trip stopped being a vacation and became something more' turning point is declared three separate times at three different milestones, each re-derived from scratch.

excerpts: Chapters Four, Six, and Nine of the (14-chapter) Day 12 entry each independently describe the same stretch of highway in similar impressionistic language.
findings.explanation: An unusually long single-day entry circles back to the same visual inventory multiple times under different chapter headings — a pacing/density issue more than a factual re-explanation.

excerpts: The van is called 'the Sprinter' / 'the van' throughout Days 1-21 — never 'Dory' in that range.
findings.explanation: Confirms the vehicle's proper name is not established until Day 22 (see EF2-07) — informational, not a redundancy problem.

excerpts: Two same-day supplemental posts appear verbatim under both Day 13 and Day 14 in the structural grouping.
findings.explanation: A data-grouping artifact from the date-co-occurrence heuristic (both days share a calendar posting date) rather than a prose-repetition problem; would create duplicate paragraphs if imported as-is.

excerpts: "This is the last off topic Captain's log. I appreciate those of you that tolerate the ramblings." (Day 35, author's own editor's note)
findings.explanation: Roughly three consecutive posts depart entirely from the expedition narrative into a business/monetization essay; the author's own in-text notes acknowledge it as a tangent — the single largest structural interruption in the archive.

excerpts: "I stopped asking, 'How much comfort can I buy?' And I started asking, 'How much time can I buy?'" (Day 32)
findings.explanation: The money=time thesis (already flagged twice in Days 1-21) is fully re-derived a third and fourth time in Days 32 and 34-35.

excerpts: "Yellowstone. Glacier. Banff. Jasper. Kluane. Wrangell-St. Elias..." (Day 32)
"Colorado. Yellowstone. Glacier. Banff. Jasper... Fairbanks. The Dalton." (Day 34)
findings.explanation: A near-identical full-route place-name list reappears six days apart, the second time with no new framing device.

excerpts: "It is the extraordinary people we meet along the way who give those places their soul." (Day 22)
"The map almost never changes you. The people do." (Day 23)
findings.explanation: Two consecutive daily entries both close on the identical 'people, not places' thesis; Day 23 restates it a second time within itself.

excerpts: "The doldrums are different. They arrive quietly..." (Day 38)
"The doldrums are patient. They never announce themselves..." (Day 39)
findings.explanation: The 'doldrums' metaphor is introduced and fully explained from scratch in the opening chapter of two consecutive entries.

excerpts: "...we slept in safe harbor." (Day 28, chapter titled 'Riding Out the Storm')
"we eased our land yacht into one more safe harbor." (Day 32, chapter titled 'Safe Harbor')
findings.explanation: Two different chapters reuse the identical phrase/title 'Safe Harbor' for structurally similar beats — a title collision risk in a compiled book with a table of contents.

excerpts: "By the time coffee was poured and Dory was ready to roll..." (Day 22, first use — no naming/origin story given)
findings.explanation: The vehicle is suddenly called 'Dory' starting Day 22 with zero introduction after being called only 'the Sprinter'/'the van' through Day 21 — a continuity gap for book editing, not a redundancy problem.

excerpts: "Put your guess in the comments. Tomorrow... I'll open the books." (Day 32, closing)
findings.explanation: Day 32 promises a cost-breakdown reveal 'tomorrow'; Day 33 never addresses it, and the figure only surfaces in passing three entries later inside an unrelated essay.
